clinicalPearls: Presents as recurrent unilateral lower abdominal or pelvic pain occurring around the middle of the menstrual cycle, roughly coinciding with ovulation
Pain classically alternates sides between cycles depending on which ovary ovulates, and typically lasts from a few hours up to a couple of days
The discomfort is usually mild to moderate and self-limiting, sometimes accompanied by light spotting or a small amount of physiological vaginal discharge
It is fundamentally a clinical diagnosis of exclusion made from a characteristic cyclical history in an otherwise well woman
Correlating symptoms with a menstrual diary and confirming the timing relative to ovulation supports the diagnosis and reassures the patient
Management is generally conservative with reassurance and simple analgesia; suppression of ovulation with a combined oral contraceptive abolishes the pain in troublesome cases
A positive pregnancy test in a woman with mid-cycle-type pain should always prompt exclusion of ectopic pregnancy rather than attribution to mittelschmerz
reference.pathophysiology: The pain is attributed to the physiological events of ovulation. Rapid stretching of the ovarian capsule by the enlarging dominant follicle, followed by rupture of the follicle, releases follicular fluid together with a small quantity of blood into the peritoneal cavity. This fluid irritates the adjacent peritoneum and may provoke localised contraction of the fallopian tube and surrounding smooth muscle, producing transient unilateral pain on the side of the ovulating ovary.
additionalInvestigations: Urinary or serum pregnancy test to exclude early or ectopic pregnancy
Transvaginal ultrasound to assess the ovaries and exclude a cyst, torsion, or free fluid
Full blood count and inflammatory markers if an infective or inflammatory cause is being considered
Urinalysis to help exclude urinary tract infection or renal tract pathology
Menstrual symptom diary correlating pain with the timing of ovulation
redFlags: A positive pregnancy test with pain, raising the possibility of ectopic pregnancy
Signs of peritonitis, haemodynamic instability, or a tender palpable mass
Fever or systemic upset suggesting infection rather than physiological pain
Progressive, severe, or atypical pain that does not follow the expected mid-cycle pattern
reference.prognosis: Mittelschmerz is a benign, self-limiting condition with an excellent outlook; symptoms resolve within a day or two each cycle and are readily controlled by ovulation suppression when they interfere with daily life.
pitfalls: Attributing pain to mittelschmerz and thereby missing an ectopic pregnancy, torsion, or appendicitis
Failing to confirm the cyclical mid-cycle pattern before making the diagnosis
Over-investigating a clear, characteristic history in an otherwise well woman
Overlooking that ovulation pain cannot occur when ovulation is suppressed, prompting a review of alternative causes
